definition: A technique for evaluating model performance by repeatedly partitioning data into different training and validation splits and averaging results across the splits.
details: Cross-validation (such as k-fold cross-validation) provides a more robust estimate of a model's generalization performance than a single train-test split, particularly useful for smaller datasets.
story: Think of a referee whose job is to be completely honest about who touched the ball last. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. It is the exam that separates “it sounds good” from “it actually is good”. What gets measured is what actually gets better. And that, done honestly, is Cross-Validation.
